newsitem.title: USA: Canada spot natgas holds in Alberta, slips in B.C.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot natgas holds in Alberta, slips in B.C.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices on Thursday were mostly steady in Alberta but softer again in British Columbia, market sources said.
Spot gas at the AECO storage in Alberta was talked at C$1.46-1.47 per gigajoule, down slightly from Wednesday's August quote at C$1.47/1.48 per GJ.
One-year AECO was still quoted at C$1.665-1.68 per GJ.
"NOVA recovered some of its linepack today," one Calgary-based trader said, noting the increased supply availability put slight pressure on the market.
Temperature highs in Calgary continue to hover around 80 degrees F, according to Weather Services Corp.
In the British Columbia market, Sumas spot prices fell another five cents to about $1.00 per million British thermal unit (mmBtu), stretching the deficit from July's index to 25 cents.
Most traders blamed the softening on an excess supply of gas in the Northwest.

At Niagara, prices were well supported by stronger gas futures and firm prices at the New York city-gate. Deals were reported done in the low-to-mid $2.30s as temperature highs in the area held in the low-80s F.
